tips.comment: The standout bet on the card for me. Has run very well in defeat, and none more so than in a decent listed contest when leading for most of the race but getting headed over the last, finishing a close 3rd. Gets 7lb from her main danger here, and the 2m 4f trip should enable her to see this out in front. Lots to like.

2nd on debut in a bumper, and it was a good race, so has shown ability even though it might not look like it, beaten some distance in 3 runs since. Still learning though and just needs to jump better.

Charming Getaway comes into this race in top form after a strong win last time, fending off a well-backed rival. He has the highest RPR in the field, suggesting he is well-handicapped and still improving. With Charlie Deutsch booked and conditions in his favor, he looks the one to beat.

Taking a punt on the Yeats handicap debutant. No idea how good he is as he's just been pootling about to get an opening mark, but 6-year-olds have a very decent record in handicap hurdles this calendar year, so worth a cheeky each way.

Could offer up a surprise if 7lb claimer works, but rides well for Twiston-Davies yard. So should be worth his salt for today's small yard and front runner who has had different ground for two runs since win.

The fact that Rocheval is still able to run in novice races should be a tip in itself. This horse is an admirable performer at the top level and definitely deserves to be the favorite here. NAP of the day.
There isn't anything between the top 2 on official ratings, and the market is giving us value as 2nd favorite. The key for me is the 4 lbs he gets, and he ran well here last time.

Ran much better on his second start over hurdles when 3rd over two miles at Ayr in January and then ran to a similar level back there next time when 4th stepped up to 20f. Jumped much better, kept to that sort of trip, at Hexham on latest start when finishing a close up 3rd. Is tried in first time cheekpieces here, kept to novice company and expected to go well.

Malicash broke his maiden at Carlisle last month after undergoing wind surgery, showing noticeable improvement. With that win under his belt, he could progress further, but he needs to step up to match the likes of Rocheval and Joecooker in this stronger field. His recent form and wind surgery suggest he has more potential to unlock.

Beat a few home in bumpers. Nothing special as of yet, but there's always room for massive improvement with such an unexposed profile. From Dan Skelton's yard, so big things can be expected. CD to suit, hopefully.

Kiwi Rush is a 5-year-old gelding trained by Harry Derham and ridden by the irrepressible Mr. P. W. Mullins, who has ridden 226 winners in Ireland in the last five years, boasting an incredible 35% win strike rate. The fact he comes to Kelso to ride a horse for a superb trainer speaks volumes. Kiwi Rush beat Japeta by 3.25 lengths on the last start and won going away. Japeta has won since, and Kiwi Rush is my short-priced banker of the day.

Out Of The Woods appeared to be a bumper of considerable promise when appearing at Ayr 75 days ago. The second horse in that race finished second at Ayr and won at Hexham in a Class 4 Bumper. This is a Class 2, which is a significant rise in class, but the breeding of Out Of The Woods shows winners after winners. We go each way as it is our best and only bet today on a super difficult Saturday.
Won a PTP in April. 5th on debut under rules in a decent bumper. Can only improve, and this race can't be much better. Has an obvious chance of improving.

Of the three runners from Lucinda Russell's yard, I like the look of Humble Jumble's debut win over course and distance. He was very well supported and beat a previous winner without being challenged - pair well clear. He obviously goes well fresh, and with a short-priced favourite, offers an appealing each-way angle.

His two runs so far have not been without promise with a 5th of 8 at Market Rasen and 6th of 16 at Doncaster last time out. He can improve based on his pedigree as he is a brother to Listed bumper winner Avakate so could improve again in what could be deemed less competitive on field size alone.
Has the profile for this yard to be sent over obstacles pretty quickly, so I am slightly surprised this horse remains in bumpers. Could be a sign and worth heeding here.
Peckforton Hills won on his second attempt at Carlisle in February. This is a wide open race with plenty of chances including the selection but he looks over priced and may be the value of the race.

Mamdoh looks the most likely winner due to his recent strong form over the C&D, including two wins in the last month. His consistency at the track, coupled with the stable’s form, makes him the standout choice.

Race 1 at Wolverhampton today is a Handicap (Class 6) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 2,815 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 4-year-old gelding Daaris from the Kevin Frost yard, and will be ridden by Mason Paetel. This son of Dawn Approach should have won more than just the two he has so far, with a total of 21 placed from 35 starts as proof thereof. This field looks ideal for him to crack his 3rd win today.

Grand Duchess Olga lines up off a mark of 60 and looks poised to go close after a solid run of staying efforts on the all-weather. She was narrowly denied over this course and distance in January, shaping like the best horse in the race before being collared late, and now gets the same conditions again. With stamina in abundance and track form to match, she sets a clear standard in a modest apprentice handicap. If given a well-judged ride, she should be bang there at the finish.
4th last time out was an improved effort for the yard. Becoming well handicapped and looks well drawn. Most of the others are out of sorts

Phoenix Beach is on the hunt for a second win this month and looks dangerous dropped back into Class 6 company off a mark of 62. He scorched home over course and distance on March 11 and ran with credit in stronger company last time despite being drawn wide. Back in calmer waters and with ideal conditions, he has the speed and form to blow this apart.

Ranking the 15 relevant recent form ratings of the entire field shows Gustav Graves as having the 8th, 5th, and 5th best ratings. 0.25pt Bet. (KEY - Wolverhampton (AW) Flat.) (5f (5f21y) Free Bets With BetUK Bet Club Handicap (Class 6) (4yo+ 0-65)).

Kept on but no extra close to home when 3rd over 6 furlongs on stable debut at Southwell 3 weeks ago. Will strip fitter following that run on the back of an absence of 71 days and could be suited by the drop in trip.
Level Up has been sitting on a very winnable mark for a while now, and his turn might come soon. Rossa Ryan is staying in the saddle. His SR for D. Evans' yard is a healthy 23%.
A chance is taken on Wedgewood, who was beaten by Defiant by a nose over course and distance 19 days ago. He could reverse form now, being better off in the weights.
They are dropping this one down in trip, class, and grade with a good jockey booking/change. A good value each way bet.

Aiming High relevant recent runs have been in 4k avg class, whereas the avg of the rest of the runners is 3.75k (Dropping in class (on average) today). Ranking the 5 relevant recent run class ratings of the entire field shows Aiming High as running in the 1st most difficult recent races. Ranking the 5 relevant recent form ratings of the entire field shows Aiming High as having the 1st best ratings. 0.25pt Bet. Bajan Blue steps into handicaps off a mark of 68 and looks very well treated based on the promise of her return at Southwell. She cruised into contention that day before the lack of a recent run told, and now steps up in trip with fitness on her side. This is a weaker race, and she’s got the profile of a filly who could leave this grade behind quickly. If she’s anywhere near as good as she looked on debut, they won’t see which way she went.
Won three starts ago. The small field will suit and has an obvious chance for me. Does need to bounce back, however, but the trip suits.

Supreme Sovereign, a three-year-old gelding trained by Charles Hills, made an impressive debut at Southwell in November 2024, defeating an experienced rival over seven furlongs. He now steps up to 1 mile 142 yards in the 6:00 PM race at Wolverhampton, carrying a penalty for his previous win. With Jason Watson retaining the ride, he looks well-positioned to maintain his unbeaten record. ￼
Been off the track for months but ran in a good maiden at Newmarket on debut, so had to be useful to be running there. Switch to AW can help and looks well-bred.

This 3 year old Maiden with 2 runs under her belt, finished 9th out of 11 at Southwell, where she was a 40/1 long shot. After a break of 138 days, she is expected to return rejuvenated, and with jockey Kieran O'Neill, who is experienced on this track, she has a good chance. A bet each-way at 100/1 could yield a nice return.

Magna Grecia Star ran well on debut running smoothly through the race, then just ran out of ideas late. Now she knows her job, steps into a soft maiden, and gets Rossa Ryan to do the steering. James Tate doesn’t waste runs at Wolverhampton, and this looks like a straightforward assignment. Expect her to cruise into it and finish the job this time.
Not sure about the trainer's SR with first-time-out horses, but this one looks well-bred and doesn't look the hardest race to be winning. The draw should help.

Beta Reader looked like a filly on the up when grinding out victory over this course and distance last week, and she’s turned out quickly under a 6-pound penalty before the handicapper can catch up. She’s uncomplicated, stays well, and clearly handles the surface, which is more than can be said for most of these. With Johnston’s yard firing and confidence high, she’s got every chance of backing it up in a race lacking much form.

An interesting looking class 5 handicap on a Saturday evening with my vote going to Maids Head a very consistent daughter of Pinatubo who was last seen at Kempton 17 days ago where finishing a very respectable 3rd/8 and is most certainly entitled to strip fitter this time out as that was her return run after a 107 day break and should also be a lot sharper at the finish this time out currently operating on an unchanged mark of 68 Maids Head looks poised to strike here and also has a handy draw coming out of gate 2 here at Wolverhampton which should put her in the perfect challenging position and as i metion above she is likely to be a lot sharper at the finish here today jockey Benoit D L Sayette takes the ride and can give Marco Botti's inmate a promising ride here at Wolverhampton very much one to consider . Respected .

Kathleen’s Glory steps into handicaps off 66 and looks like a classic Gosden project??'three quiet runs, now ready to show her hand. She’s bred to be better than this grade and gets a very winnable opening mark for her first go in a nursery field. With cheekpieces on for the first time and the yard in strong form, this could be the night she makes her move.

Party Bear showed promising form with a strong finish for second on its 6f handicap debut at Wolverhampton. The step up to 7f should suit, and it could improve further with that experience. With good potential and recent improvement, Party Bear is a strong contender here.
Three runs so far and has shown promise. Very unexposed, so can still improve bundles. The draw will help, as will the CD.

I can't resist a small each way bet on this well-drawn horse, which has shown nothing in his last two runs. But prior to that, he was a half-length second on his only previous run over course and distance. The horse led until late on and races off the same mark here. Clearly, a reproduction of that form would make a mockery of the 50/1 quote here. He even has the favorable low draw again, so hopefully, he'll set the pace again and attempt to fend off the late challengers.

Sceptic finally clicked last time, storming clear over this trip here just 11 days ago, and now turns up under a 5-pound penalty that still leaves him below last year’s peak. He travelled like a different horse that day and looked full of running past the line, suggesting there’s more to come now he’s found his rhythm. In a race full of out-of-form types, he arrives with momentum and confidence and looks set for a big run.

234 form figures recently, so it does need to improve again to win. But it was winning races before that, and this CD is likely to suit. The main market dangers haven't been in the best of form recently.
Off the mark from 7 lb lower over 8.5f here a few starts back. Credible second over 9.5f here two starts ago. That looked a better race than this, although a career best is needed to win.

This actually looks like a tricky race to make a selection. A few have wins under their belts and a couple are newcomers. Opting for Tiddesley Wood, who made a good start to racing on debut in January, finishing third in a bumper at Doncaster.

Yard 23-86 at a decent 27% strike rate in bumpers this season so anything they run has to be respected in this sphere. Add in the fact a further 28 of those 86 have placed too then it's fair to say this one looks a huge ew player here. Really caught the eye on debut when taking on a an experience rival and travelled really well in last place before moving nicely up to chase home the battle hardened winner. Dam only raced twice and did win on second start after finishing 2nd on debut and has produced a chase winner in France already. Sure to improve and looks sure to go close despite this looking very competitive.

TALK TO THE MAN has won a point-to-point race at 3f. Fifth in a NH flat race over 2m 1f at Exeter on his latest outing in January. Course distance and going should suit and he could well be able to win this race.

This is always a very good bumper and was won last year by the highly promising Regents Stroll. There are some very promising looking horses, but I really like the look of My Fortune who has a great pedigree. He is by Milan, out of a Bob Back mare who has produced plenty of good horses. He has been entered numerous times over recent weeks so should be ready to do himself justice in this hot contest.
Klub De Reve was 7th of 16 at Doncaster in January making his stable debut. With Harry Derham in excellent form a chance is taken that he will improve on his second run for the stable.

J J O'Neill has a beautiful, well-bred bay gelding having his first outing in a National Hunt flat race on what I presume is good ground. Western George is by Order Of St George, whose progeny have been giving him a good vibe this season with winners appearing. Western George's dam sire is Westerner, who is also producing very useful progeny. With these genes in Western George's blood, Richie McLernon could be nursing his charge home with a big run appearing, and at 28/1, he might be under the radar.
Javert Allen stands out as a solid contender. He won 2 of 3 chase starts, only narrowly beaten last time when setting too strong a pace.

BEAU BALKO has won two hurdle races and two chases from 2m to 2m 4f. Fourth in a chase over 2m 4f at Newbury on his latest outing earlier this month. Dropped in trip to 2m should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to win this race.

Teddy Blue followed his Huntingdon win with a three and a half length triumph at Kempton last week and is quickly turned out off a four lb higher rating. Harry Derham's seven-year-old makes only his fourth chase start and could have plenty more to offer so he can complete the hat-trick.
Got some headgear on today, which could improve him. Was 4th last time out, and that's not good enough. Needs to improve, but it's possible for a good trainer.
They're dropping this one back down in trip with the regular jockey back on board. Worth a small each-way saver bet.
Possible two-horse race as the other market leader has won its last two. This one, for me, has more improvement in the tank left and a good trainer-jockey combo.

The trainer appears resurgent and the rider has stepped into the limelight in the last few months. On for a treble and the drying ground will suit. Up only 5 points for the latest win and that won't stop further progress.

Another horse who prefers a sounder surface, which he gets today. He's just 2 lbs above his last winning mark, which should help. Although admittedly, he's never won off a mark this high, his overall form would suggest this mark certainly isn't beyond him. He tends to run well at this track. He also boasts a CD win, which helps, of course, having won this race off a 10 lbs lower mark last term. His form this season would suggest he can defy that 10 lbs higher mark. He won a competitive handicap at Chepstow on reappearance, finding plenty to fend off Pull Again Green. He then finished a decent 3rd behind Chianti Classico at Ascot off a 2 lbs higher mark than this, beaten just 4L. His most recent run was okay, finishing a beaten 2nd behind Tightenourbelts. That horse was well in off that mark, plus this fella carried 12 st, so no disgrace there. If he runs his race, he should be thereabouts.

SOME SCOPE has won a hurdle race and three chases from 3m to 3m 1f. Also won a point-to-point race. Pulled up in a chase over 3m 2f at Doncaster on his latest outing earlier this month. Dropped in trip to 2m 7f should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to win this race.

This 3-year-old colt made a winning racecourse debut for trainer R. Varian over one mile at this course 15 days ago. He ran on well in the closing stages despite showing signs of greenness to beat the well-backed K. R. Burke-trained Nordic Norm by 2 1/4 lengths. With improvement likely and J. Mitchell back in the saddle, he can follow up today.
Ran very green on his debut at this course six weeks ago and did well to get 2nd in the end, beaten a head. The horse that won has since finished 2nd behind Rahiebb. Has a chance.
Something amiss last time out, went backwards from debut 3rd. If recapturing that form, should be bang there today. Billy is on board.

Too Much is interesting at the top of the weights here. Last time out he tackled a stronger to 75 contest and didn’t disgrace himself at all, finishing just over three lengths behind the winner despite having traffic issues in the straight. That was off 66 and he runs off 65 here, plus he’s got a capable 5lb claimer on board, so he’s effectively 6lb better off for that effort. His sole win came over 7f but he’s shaped like a mile will suit, especially if he’s allowed to sit handier. This drop in class feels significant. He’s been running with credit in better company and now faces a field where a repeat of that last run could see him right in the mix. If the pace is fair and he gets a smoother passage, he should go close.
Stable in blinding form, mainly due to this runner who has turned out three times in eight days earlier in the month. Only beaten in a photo latest and figures to go close again.

Winner over a mile here in January. Somewhat inconsistent since, but ran okay when not beaten far in 5th last time and is of interest this evening on this rare drop to 7 furlongs, as won over course and distance off 7lb higher just over a year ago.

Trais Fluors is a real veteran and not without a touch of class, especially in a race like this. He’s a nine-time winner, including in Listed company back in the day, and while those days are behind him, he’s still more than capable at this sort of level. His recent efforts suggest there’s still some spark when he stayed on steadily over 7f here last time in a race that wasn’t really run to suit, and stepping back up to a mile looks the right move. He’s now 2lb lower than when fourth in a stronger to 75 back in January, and this to 65 is a fair bit weaker on paper. He’s well drawn to sit handy if they want, and the booking of a jockey who knows him well is no bad thing. He’ll need things to fall right, but for me he’s got the back class to make him interesting at a nice price. Not one to rule out lightly.
Didn't take to hurdling. Before that, had decent form on the flat, including winning over course and distance. Today's jockey, Paul Mulrennan, has previously ridden and placed on Code Purple.
Has many wins, but all over 6f for this stable. But has won at the trip before for a different yard and has the speed to win this. Well drawn.

Inns Of Fear is stepping onto the Newcastle track with a fair bit of buzz. This colt showed promise over in Ireland, snagging a second place at Dundalk over a mile. Now under the guidance of George Boughey and sporting a first-time tongue strap, he's dropping back to 6 furlongs, which could be right up his alley. With Billy Loughnane taking the reins, there's a sense that Inns Of Fear is primed for a strong performance.

Sharon Curly showed a marked improvement on her second run over course and distance three weeks ago when she placed third. She has been upped in the weights but could build on that run and hit the frame again.
Found a good amount of pace on her last outing at the end of February to post a useful 2nd place. Shapes as though she might go well in this low grade handicap and has to be a good E/W option.

Gelded son of Magna Grecia who was last seen at this venue over the mile trip 12 days ago where finishing 8th/9 however I'm willing to excuse that run as he looked to be in need of it as he was returning from a 80 day break on the occasion currently operating on a falling mark of 50 Nigel Tinkler's inmate is well off the handicappers radar and it is very well possible he is better than a mark of 50 heading down the handicap route in very good time as he is off the handicappers radar for the time being it would be a wise and profitable move to catch him running well at this stage as he is a valuable looking E/W price at the time of writing jockey Billy Loughnane takes the ride that being a positive booking . Respected .

Miakoda's been knocking on the door for a while now, hasn't he? This 3yo gelding has been in the mix, placing in three of his eleven starts. While he hasn't quite found that winning formula yet, his consistent performances suggest he's got the potential to break his maiden soon.
Got stuck and had to check at the completely wrong time in the last race, and I think the performance can be upgraded here. Great each way chance.

Hardlass relevant recent runs have been in 3k avg class, whereas the avg of the rest of the runners is 3.95k (Going up in class (on average) today). Ranking the 27 relevant recent run class ratings of the entire field shows Hardlass as running in the 14th, and 14th most difficult recent races. Ranking the 27 relevant recent form ratings of the entire field shows Hardlass as having the 4th, and 2nd best ratings. 0.25pt Bet. (KEY - Newcastle (AW) Flat.) (7f (7f14y) BetMGM: It's Showtime Handicap (Class 6) (3yo 0-55)).'
5th on handicap debut, probably in a similar race here. Needs to improve, but hood is fitted and trainer does well here.

Triple Wishes makes her handicap debut off a mark of 55 following three quiet runs in maiden company, though her latest fourth at Newcastle offered a glimmer of promise. Beaten three lengths in a small field over six furlongs, she shaped as though a stronger pace and extra distance could unlock more. Her pedigree, by Expert Eye out of Three Coins, points toward improvement at seven furlongs. The first-time hood could help her settle, and in a weak race with no standout form, she has the profile of one who might progress now switched to handicaps.

The standout contender looks to be Mayo County. He won convincingly over this course and distance last time, has course form, and is improving. Despite the 7lb rise, he remains well-treated and should go close again.

Rebecca's Girl has been a model of consistency over the winter and she deserves another 1 against her name. She's a C&D winner and looks best over 6f/7f and if she can get to the front she might just take some stopping today.

Lord Abama, a six-year-old gelding trained by Michael Dods, has shown consistent form over six furlongs at Newcastle. His latest win came on November 5, 2024, in a Class 6 handicap over this course and distance off a mark of 62. He is now rated 65, just 3 pounds higher, indicating he remains competitively handicapped. Notably, he has secured three wins and eight placings from 28 starts, reflecting a respectable 11% win rate. His familiarity with the track and proven ability at the distance suggest he could be a strong contender in the upcoming Class 5 event.

Comes here from a slipping mark and sports blinkers for the first time. Given too much to do when beaten just over a length over 5f around here on the penultimate start. Outpaced that day, this step up in trip from a 3lb lower mark gives him an each-way chance.
Goes well fresh. Has put in big efforts in the past. Recent form was poor, but given a break and could surprise at big odds here.

Urban Dandy comes here in red-hot form, having bolted up over a mile at Newcastle just 12 days ago off a mark of 48. That win came on the back of a narrow second at the same venue, and he now bids for a quick double under just a 5-pound penalty. Dropping to seven furlongs poses no issue given how strongly he travelled last time, and he remains well treated against this level of opposition. With confidence high and conditions ideal, he looks the one to beat.
Right there on the numbers in this classified race with half the field deadwood. Moves back up to 7f. Chance in a very poor race.
Won two starts back. Has won over this distance in the past also, so it's no problem. Probably just needs slight improvement to be seen winning again here. Well drawn.

Dandy Lichious is threatening to strike after two eye-catching thirds over seven furlongs, including a strong finish here at Newcastle in January where he was closing late from off the pace. He’s now just 1 pound above his last winning mark, which came over this trip at Dundalk, and looks primed to deliver with conditions to suit. With the race likely to set up for a closer, he shapes as a big player in a modest Class 6.

Three time course winner around this time last year. Signs on the last two runs that he is returning to form. First time blinkers on and that could bring out an improvement. The trainer has had two winners from his last six runners.

7-year-old gelding sired by Adaay runs well on this surface. Hasn't been out for 144 days, so fitness is taken on trust, but down into a classified event where he normally runs in handicaps. Could surprise at a decent price first time back.

Dark Kestrel is thriving at present and looks a major player dropping back into Class 5 company. He ran a cracker here nine days ago in a Class 4, flashing home for second behind a progressive type and confirming he’s still on the up off a mark of 74. That followed a solid run in a strong field and a course win in the autumn, making him one of the most consistent five-furlong operators on the all-weather this winter. Back at his optimum trip and track, he sets the standard and rates a live contender.
2-2 at the track, but it's at 6f. Anyway, must have plenty of speed and can easily take this if back to that form.

Ganesha looks like a solid contender after benefiting from a wind operation in December, which led to an improved performance and a C&D victory 15 days ago. The horse has already beaten some of today’s rivals, showing strong form on the all-weather. With proven ability over 5f and a stable that has found the key to unlocking its potential, Ganesha has a strong chance of following up with another win.

Darlo Pride has been running consistently well, finishing in the top four in his last three outings. He handles these conditions well and remains competitive off his current mark. While he hasn’t won recently, his reliable form suggests he could be in the mix once again.
Won over course and distance on penultimate start in Class 6 company. 3rd of 8 beaten 2 lengths in Class 4 9 days ago and can make his presence felt eased in grade to this Class 5.
Golden Rainbow has won 5 times on all-weather tracks, 4 over course and distance (and finished third here last time out). Each way chance.

South Shore's form on paper does look off putting however looks can be deceiving and a deeper analysis of this individual tells a whole different story was last seen at this venue racing at the 6 furlong trip where finishing last of 8 however he was returning from a 152 day break and most certainly needed that run likely to be more adjusted back home as he joined this yard last year from the Karl Burke stable and he did win of a mark of 75 with that stable he is now operating on mark 68 now surely a 4yo gelded son of Blue Point who was capable of winning of a mark of 75 last year is likely to have a very big performance in the locker of a mark of 68 and he did switch yards at a crucial stage of his career a monster E/W price at the time of writing he is worth the interest and if on song as he should be he could cause a shock in the finale and if he is to settle for a silver medal at the very least it wouldn't be so bad given the odds on offer

This one goes straight into the 'e/w bet to nothing' category for me since he's going to be very hard to keep out of the frame under his ideal conditions. He's very ground dependent and the drying ground is going to really suit. He has 2 pulled-up efforts on soft this season, but in the other races on better ground, he's finished 2-2-3-1. The horse was a length 2nd on his only other run over C&D where the winner was thrown in since he's since won off a 15lb higher mark. Fearless Action has a 6lb rise to defy but is in great heart, and the first-time booking of Gavin Sheehan is a positive. He has won 5 times from just 12 rides at the course in the last year.
Has to give piles of weight away because he's rated 148, but he can take this if jumping better. 5 wins from 17 over fences, and that's better than some. Small field to suit.
